answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove elapsed computation by completing a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with a Wesolowski proof enabling efficient verification. GPUs can process separate chains in parallel, but cannot shortcut the dependency within any one chain, so every clone still incurs a physical time bottleneck; multiplying identities multiplies the work. No wander across a knoll or copper-fast shortcut evades that delay.
